sentences.text: The genus Ruixinia includes only one known species, Ruixinia zhangi, which possessed a neck exceeding four meters in length supported by at least fifteen cervical vertebrae.
Its tail features fused vertebrae forming a rodlike structure, while the chevrons are distinctive, including a twenty-first caudal vertebra with a pentagonal shape.
The holotype specimen preserves the most complete series of tail vertebrae known from any Asian titanosauriform.
Fused tail vertebrae create a unique rodlike structure not commonly seen in other dinosaurs.
The holotype was discovered in the Yixian Formation at Beipiao, Liaoning Province, northeastern China, a site dated to the Barremian age of the Early Cretaceous period.
The species name honors Ruixin Zhang, a contributor to the Erlianhaote Dinosaur Museum.
Han et al. (2024) recovered Ruixinia as a member of the Euhelopodidae, placing it as the sister taxon to Jiangshanosaurus within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
Ruixinia is a member of the Jehol Biota and lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
The time range for Ruixinia extends from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.

It is debated whether Ruixinia is a titanosaur, as some researchers suggest affinities with mamenchisaurids based on similarities with Mamenchisaurus, while Averianov and colleagues (2025) proposed that Ruixinia is a non-lithostrotian titanosaur based on the anatomy of its anterior caudal vertebrae.
